t: That each circuit judge and each district judge may appoint a secretary, and each senior circuit judge and each senior district judge in districts having five or more district judges may also appoint an assistant secretary, who shall, subject to appropriations to be made by the Congress, receive compensation to be fixed from time to time by the Director of the Administrative Office of the United States courts and shall be reimbursed for their actual traveling expenses and expenses incurred for subsistence, within the limitations prescribed by law, when necessarily absent from their designated posts of duty on official business.

fable.w: This section authorizes federal judges to appoint secretaries and assistant secretaries, with compensation set by the Director of the Administrative Office of the United States Courts. The tempting reading is that 'appoint' implies bringing in outsiders, but the appointees are paid federal judicial employees, not outside parties consulted on a federal decision. Every actor is inside the federal government, and there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue.
fable.s: each circuit judge and each district judge may appoint a secretary

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes federal judges to appoint secretaries and assistant secretaries. These appointees are employees of the federal judiciary, which is part of the federal government. There is no involvement of outside parties, such as the public, states, or private entities, in the decision-making process described. The text deals solely with internal staffing and compensation within the government.
qwen_block.s: That each circuit judge and each district judge may appoint a secretary, and each senior circuit judge and each senior district judge in districts having five or more district judges may also appoint an assistant secretary

opus.w: This section lets federal judges hire secretaries, who are paid federal employees. Their pay is set by the Director of the Administrative Office, subject to appropriations by Congress. Every actor is inside the federal government, so no outside party is consulted or involved in a federal decision. Appointing staff is not participation, just as in the NLRB example.
opus.s: each circuit judge and each district judge may appoint a secretary
opus.b: Someone might read "appoint" and "secretary" as bringing outside people into a decision. That reading fails. The secretaries become paid federal court employees, and everyone else involved (judges, Congress, the Director of the Administrative Office) is inside the federal government. Nothing here involves an outside party in a federal decision.
